parsed.g: Find and report the total number of reviews in the store that mention the term 'decent'
P_t: Navigated to Marketing section in Magento Admin (step 1)
Navigated to All Reviews page under Marketing > User Content (step 2)
Located the Review filter textbox in the reviews table (step 3)
R_t: Successfully type 'decent' into the Review filter textbox and apply the search filter
Count and report the number of reviews returned that mention 'decent'
parsed.e_t: The ground-truth DOM shows the admin session has expired or been lost — the current page is the Magento Admin login page (adminhtml-auth-login), not the Reviews page. The page contains a login form with username and password fields, not the reviews management interface the agent believes it is on.
C: The agent must re-authenticate to the Magento Admin panel before it can access the Reviews section
The agent should use the Review column filter to search for 'decent' once logged in
The search should be performed on the All Reviews page under Marketing > User Content > Reviews

F_t.cause: The text 'decent' was appended to existing text in the field, resulting in 'satisfdecentied' as shown in the DOM gridcell content at step 4, rather than replacing the field content with just 'decent'
Search was performed with corrupted filter value 'satisfdecentied' instead of 'decent', resulting in 0 records found

Despite using clear=1 flag, the DOM at step 6 still shows the Review filter gridcell labeled 'satisfdecentied' with an empty textbox, indicating the type action did not properly update the filter value

The ground-truth DOM at step 6 shows the page has reverted to the admin login page, meaning the session expired. The agent is no longer on the Reviews page and the action targeted a non-existent element ID

K_t: The Reviews page is accessible via Marketing > User Content > All Reviews in Magento Admin
The Review column filter textbox is used to search for reviews containing specific text
The admin session has expired — the current ground-truth DOM shows the login page, not the Reviews page
Previous attempts to filter by 'decent' failed because the filter field contained 'satisfdecentied' (corrupted text from appending rather than replacing)
The correct approach requires: login again, navigate to Marketing > User Content > All Reviews, clear the Review filter field, type 'decent', and click Search
